name: optquery_cells
hypothesis: The champion ranks the pool against question + all four options through a CLIP text tower with a 77-token limit and truncation=True, so on most Video-MME rows options C and D never reach the encoder and every one of its 50 frames is chosen by a systematically half-blind signal. Issue five short queries instead (the question alone, and each option clause alone with its letter prefix stripped), fuse all ten rankings by RRF for the hypothesis-neutral coverage grid, and deal the 15-frame reserve ROUND-ROBIN across hypotheses so each option gets ~3 dedicated witnesses and a distractor can be ruled out on frames chosen to support it. Frame-neutral at exactly 50; the only cost is 10 retrieval calls instead of 2.

name: bill_dense160
hypothesis: A flat 160-frame bill (+67% on the parent's 96.0, +220% on the 50-frame backbone). Three constants are now measured on this lineage - 28 -> 69.8, 50 -> 73.56, 96 -> 70.9 - and read together they say the frame curve has an interior peak rather than the saturating monotone the warm phase assumed (+1.07 pp per doubling). But 96 sits only 2.66 pp below 50 against a 1.93 pp paired noise floor, so one point cannot tell a real inverted-U from a shallow plateau with a noisy dip on it; doubling the distance from the peak settles it. The mechanism that must bend the curve is the pixel total: the Qwen3-VL video processor budgets pixels as a TOTAL over the clip (t*h*w <= 25165824), so the per-frame allowance falls as 1/t - about 512x928 at 50, 384x672 at 96, 296x528 at 160 - and the config's per-frame default of 230400 is slack at every one of those counts, so the total is what binds and 160 is squarely inside the acuity-starved region nothing has reached. Both outcomes are worth having: ~70 makes the region above 50 a broad flat shelf and frames stay a saturating covariate; below ~67 makes it an inverted-U, which means every cross-branch regression carrying frames as linear-in-log is misspecified on its right half. STATED BEFORE THE RUN: mean(num_frames) = 160.0 exactly - verified in the prototype at every duration in the split's range (34 s to 3400 s), no pool starvation and no max_frames clipping (cap is 768). Selection rule byte-identical to the backbone (sha256 of the _queries/_select region matches optquery_cells, and matches bill_wide96 and tempo_ration96); the only line the diff writes is the bill. At 160 the parent's own rule reallocates itself - 112 coverage cells leave the 0.5 s reserve gap unsatisfiable on short videos so the uniform backfill finishes the read - and that is the parent's expression evaluating at a new total, not a second change.

name: stemanchor_cells
hypothesis: change the QUERY SET the rankings are read from, in the opposite direction to distinctq_cells: the backbone asks each retriever for a bare option clause, which is a fine query when the clause is a scene description and barely a query at all for the categories this branch is worst on — a counting question's clauses are '2','3','4','5' and an attribute question's are 'red','blue', strings whose CLIP embedding names no visual content, so the cell that elects from that ranking elects the tower's response to a numeral; the stem holds exactly what is missing (what is being counted, whose colour, before what) and the backbone sends it only as a separate sixth-of-the-evidence query, never combined with any one hypothesis, so a hypothesis query becomes its clause FIRST — the backbone's own 77-token lesson, so the anchor can never cost the hypothesis itself — then the stem's content words the clause does not already contain, in stem order, until a joint 32-word budget is spent; the index list now data-depends on the set of stem content words ABSENT from a given clause and on that clause's own length, which makes the rule self-regulating rather than uniform ('3' is anchored with the whole focus and becomes '3 people wearing hats', a clause that is already a sentence takes a word or two, a clause at or over the budget is passed through verbatim), the query count and the ten retrieval calls are unchanged, and an empty stem, an all-function-word stem or clauses that already contain every content word return the backbone's queries string for string (prototype: queries printed for counting / attribute / event / over-budget stems, word budget respected, all three degenerate stems reproduce the parent exactly)

name: casting_call
hypothesis: slotB_roles_off measured the preamble as the largest single family effect on the run (-9.33 pp), but on this backbone every cast has smuggled a second treatment in beside the persona — a reshaped output format, halved evidence, an override rule — and purevote_screen, the cleanest read so far, used a header that was a constant chosen by the author and identical on all 450 questions. Here the header IS the decision and nothing else moves. A free casting director sees the question with no candidate answers and a free option reader sees the clauses with the question withheld; both are asked for the same kind of product, a two-or-three-word name for the kind of viewer this needs, from evidence that shares no words. Concord (their nominations share a content word) casts that specialist; discord means nobody knows what kind of watching this is and purevote_screen's anonymous answerer stands byte for byte. Same 50 frames, same ctx.mc_prompt(), same decoder in both branches — the two paths differ only in the words after "You are the"

name: crossorder_triad
hypothesis: The parent's three members decorrelate only through the frame sample, and that axis is exhausted (plurality over three strong members averages 72.6 against 73.6 for the best single member; the parent's +1.7 is the maximum of 4000 drawable triples). A common-mode error remains that the vote structurally cannot touch: gold is nearly flat across the letters (A 107, B 115, C 112, D 93) while the model is not (uniform answers B 142 times, the parent 133), and all three members read the identical option list in the identical order, so a position-driven choice is unanimous by construction. Each member is therefore handed its own option permutation -- as given, reversed, rotated by half -- and the plurality is taken in CONTENT space, so every option occupies three different slots and a slot-driven choice now disagrees with itself where the gate can see it. order_invariance (67.1 from clip_topk 66.2) is the only frame-free mechanism in the archive with a positive delta and has never been lifted onto a strong backbone. Cost shape is the parent's exactly.

name: rift_mix_router
hypothesis: Every framework here fills its budget by one fixed recipe that assumes its own retrieval inputs are trustworthy, and never asks per question whether they are -- yet the geometry says so for free, before any pixel is read. CONCORD (clip_base vs clip_large top-24 overlap on the same pool) says whether the fused ranking every framework trusts is meaningful or arbitrary; TANGLE (mean pairwise overlap of the four per-option top-24 sets) says whether the options are visually separable at all, which is precisely when a per-option quota is worth buying and why option_balance's unconditional version scored 66.0. Width is pinned EXACTLY at the parent's -- frame count is the dominant confound and this candidate must not touch it -- and the geometry decides the mix inside it: a quarter scaled by (1-concord) goes to the contested frames exactly one encoder believes in (RRF over the symmetric difference), a quarter scaled by (1-tangle) goes round-robin to the per-option rankings, and at least half stays the parent's stratified ranked fill so the coverage floor that scout_then_read lost is never breached. Verified in the rig: with no rift and no separability the frame set is byte-identical to iso_token_span, and with signal it differs on 19 of 60 frames at exactly the same count.

name: isotoken_pool_read
hypothesis: UP in frames, FLAT in tokens -- the missing bracket at the top. Every frames-vs-accuracy reading on this branch confounds coverage with compute, and the two brackets that exist sit at the bottom (plain 23.3 -> 61.1 against iso-token 15.7 -> 61.1) and the middle (plain 109.05 -> 69.8 against iso-token 122.20 -> 69.1). Above 122 there is none, which is exactly where the headline sits: sublinear_pool_law's 70.9 at 159.76 frames is bought with roughly three times the backbone's visual tokens. Do not change the bill; change the split. The backbone's two lines are reciprocal (widen by m, refund base_pixels/m), so its pass carries the same ~7.4 Mpx on every video whatever its length. State the finest acuity the read may fall to and let the width be the largest number of frames that bill affords at it. The acuity is not an invented constant: it is the 224x224 input resolution of the CLIP encoder that ranked and selected these frames, so the read is never coarser than the evidence that chose it, and the achieved acuity is then recovered from the width so the token identity is exact. Because the bill is constant across videos so is the width -- the branch's first number that does not move with length at all. Expected mean ~140 frames vs 54.57 (+157%): 146 on any video cut into 9 or more stretches, less only on the sparsely cut ones, at ~50176 px/frame (~64 visual tokens per frame, a quarter of the pool default). Same token bill as the backbone, 2.6x its frames, and matched frames against sublinear_pool_law at a third of its tokens. If it holds ~70 the top of the plateau is bought with coverage and the compute is free; if it falls to ~64 the plateau is a token effect and the run's rho +0.52 between frames and accuracy is largely arithmetic. Noted honestly: this is acuity_swap_read's token identity run in the opposite direction -- that one stated a high acuity and let the width fall out at 15.7 -- and the branch needs the up-slope end of the same line.

name: jumpfill_memo
hypothesis: MEMORY half, a GROUNDED note at the smallest levy a grounded note can cost. The branch now knows why its budget-neutral memory candidates lost, and it is not the notes: chunkcarry_tally scored 43.3% on the 67 questions where it fired against 55.2% for the same allocation answered in one pass, and probe_recall_split took 8 of 64 frames off the answering pass and lost 6.4pp on long videos. Both starved the answer. optioncue_memo starved nothing but took its note from a text-only pass that had never seen the video, so the note was speculation about the options (66.4). The untried corner is a note that is GROUNDED with a levy as small as a levy can be: Qwen's processor takes a two-frame clip, so a grounded probe costs exactly 2 metered frames and the answer pass gives up exactly 2, keeping 62 of 64. If a grounded note is worth anything it is worth two frames; if it is not worth two, it is not worth any, which makes this the maximum-power test of the whole memory half. Chain: motion() values -> per-gap change mass -> (a) the frame pair straddling the largest unseen jump, probed as a pair; (b) the two frames whose removal merges the two EMPTIEST gaps, dropped to pay for it -> ctx.memory.note(the probe's raw reply) -> ctx.memory.digest(340) in the answer prompt. One quantity does both jobs: gapmass_ledger (70.0) computes the same per-gap mass and can only POINT at the jump, while this sends the model to look at the two frames on either side and carries back what it says. Every test is a multiple of an equal share of THIS video's change - the jump must hold more than twice one, each dropped frame must cost less than one - so nothing is tuned per corpus, and reserved frames, the pair itself, the two stack endpoints and any two frames adjacent in the stack are all excluded from the levy. SALIENCE IS DESIGNED, NOT DEFAULT: two notes, the model's own words at the jump's share of the video's change and the framework's arithmetic at zero, under a salience policy whose budget the pair exceeds only when the model actually said a lot - so a talkative reply evicts the arithmetic and keeps the observation (verified: ev=1, only the observation reaches the digest), a terse one keeps both. Truncation discipline: the reply is cut back to its last complete sentence WITHIN the note budget, so a run-on that never finishes a sentence carries nothing rather than putting half a word in front of the frames. VERIFIED FRAME COUNT: 2 + (width - 2) = width - metered 2+62=64 and 2+30=32 across 45 configs - and exactly the backbone's single pass on every unfired path, verified as a cache-hit identity on the all-empty stub. mem.writes=2 and mem.reads=1 on the note path; both 0 with the plain prompt on the empty, bare-fragment and run-on paths. No extra tool calls or renders; two grounded passes against a budget of twelve, and the probe carries no mc_prompt so first_pred still comes from the answer pass. Fired on 36/45 configs. HONEST CAVEAT: the two frames are spent before the reply is read, so a failed probe answers on width-2 with the plain prompt and never buys them back - that path is a strict 2-frame loss against the backbone, which is the price of measuring this corner at all.

name: field_plateau_runs
hypothesis: Every rule on this axis, the backbone included, treats a slot as a point: one frame, one moment, next slot to the next candidate. Nobody has read the one thing the field says about an ALREADY CHOSEN frame - how long the relevance around it lasts. So run the backbone's ranked stratified fill verbatim and ask each accepted frame one further question: how long does the field around it hold at least halfway between its own relevance and the MEDIAN of its stretch? That duration, divided by the backbone's own min-gap (the resolution at which it already refuses to call two frames different moments), is how many further slots stay with the frame, spread across its run and paid for out of the same stretch quota. A spike, or a frame no better than ordinary for its stretch, is a single point and the ranked list continues, which is the backbone verbatim. The level is measured against the stretch median rather than the peak's flanking valleys on purpose: a rank-inverted field wiggles, and the half-prominence contour of a wiggle riding on a broad swell is one sample wide however broad the swell is, so that variant measures rank noise instead of duration (verified: it fires on 2 of ~300 modes and moves 3% of slots, against 8% for this one). Width is spent on continuity exactly where continuity is missing, and the per-stretch quotas keep the coverage floor intact by construction.

name: episode_rate_read
hypothesis: The champion is the one framework that moved the frame RATE rather than the placement, but it funds exactly ONE contiguous run and sizes it from the tightest interval covering the whole top of the ranking, so a question whose evidence is two or three separated moments has no interval that covers it, the reserve is refused outright and the read falls back to the uniform-rate skeleton. Run the parent's own window search AGAIN on what is left: fund the tightest interval the remaining reserve can resolve, charge it the parent's rate test as a per-run entrance fee, strike its ranked frames out and look again. The number of runs is never chosen -- it is however many the reserve can still afford -- and the leftover is dealt one frame at a time to the run with the most ranked mass per frame it holds, so a one-moment video puts the whole reserve on one run and lands where the parent lands, while two or three moments split. Targets the two buckets that are the floor of this benchmark and that both need a moment seen as a moment: Counting 46.8% and Temporal Reasoning 50.0%, 79 of 450 questions. Iso-frame with cell_c and with the parent (one grounded pass, same width, same pixels, one extra retrieval call at the parent's own depth), so any difference is the rate.

name: slotC_retrieve_up_pq
hypothesis: SLOT C on retrieve, the only family whose removal costs anything on this line (-6.6, against -0.2 for perceive and -0.2 for the second grounded pass). A dose curve for it exists — 0 calls 62.7, 5 calls 67.8, 11 calls 69.3, 22 calls 68.2 — but every point was measured on the OLD query mechanism, where view A pushed question+all four options into CLIP's 77-token window and had it truncated. The champion replaced that query wholesale with model-written caption-shaped phrases and gained a point, and a curve measured on a query that never reached the encoder does not transfer to one that does, so the champion's ~18 calls is a single unanchored point. This is the up end on the new mechanism: the dial is the number of DISTINCT QUERIES, doubled in both views. View A goes 4 planned phrases to 8 at a constant 20 output tokens per phrase (80 to 160), so the planner is not being truncated into a different mechanism. View B asks each option both as question+option (the parent's query) and as the bare option text, the caption-shaped form of the same hypothesis and the distribution CLIP was trained on: 4 option queries to 8. ~18 retrieve calls to 34 of a 60 budget. Held fixed: reserved slots per view stay at 8 (8 hypotheses x quota 1 instead of 4 x quota 2), per_query_k, both views emitting exactly num_frames, the consensus stop, the union escalation, and therefore the ~38 frame budget — frame count is the strongest confound here and a sweep that moved it would measure the budget instead of the family. Flat or down says query breadth is past its useful point; up says four phrases were leaving headroom.

name: bd_appeal_rate
hypothesis: Size the appeal by how much video there is to appeal over. Parent's selection, screens (16/16, byte-for-byte) and appeal band [58,104] are all kept; the ONLY change is the argument mapped into that band -- coverage hole becomes extent: k_e = even(58 + 46*min(1, total_frames/54000)), giving 60/70/104 on short/medium/long. The branch has now put three arguments into essentially the same band (overlap 71.3, coverage hole 71.8, option similarity 71.8) with escalator accuracies 63.6/65.5/65.5 off unions of 90.7/107.5/96.0, so appeal SIZE moves accuracy hard (49.6% at a 19-frame union, 65.5% at ~100) and appears to saturate near 100. Nobody has asked whether that saturation point is a COUNT or a DENSITY: 100 frames of a 90-second clip is more than one per second and past saturation, 100 frames of 40 minutes is one per 24 seconds and is not. Also the natural cross of the branch's two measured wins -- bd_rate_perminute put length on the SCREENS (-0.6pp), bd_appeal_wide put frames on the APPEAL (+0.9pp), and length has never been put on the appeal, the only pass where frames demonstrably pay. Screens unchanged means the two letters and the 110/450 = 0.2444 escalation set are exactly the parent's and both screening passes are cache hits, so mean = 32 + 0.2444*E|A' u B'| >= 32 + 0.2444*58 = 46.2 by construction, past >=45.9 with no distributional assumption. Expected 55-62; probe_iter4 meters 56.0-63.7.

name: pg_evidence_audit
hypothesis: the can-overturn-a-majority arm, priced at zero frames: each read names its deciding evidence in the same pass, and on agreement a text-only ask_vlm auditor may override the consensus from those two cited observations; the 352-question agreeing slice holds 89 of 133 errors and the backbone never revisits it

name: sl_where_to_look
hypothesis: Two untried things. (1) The record as an attention POINTER, not a description: ctx.tools.similarity ranks the frames the pass is already about to look at against the QUESTION itself - not the options, not a whole-video search - so the note is one clause saying which of the moments in front of the model the question is actually about. The warm phase's most productive use of memory was a pointer rather than a summary of what was seen, and no candidate here has written one. (2) Eviction as an ADJUDICATOR rather than a compressor: a rank carries no score, so the pointer's confidence comes from replication - the two views are retrieved from different queries, and if both independently put their best frame at the same point on the clock the pointer has replicated. The ledger holds the pointer at salience = that replication against a rival note asserting the frames are undifferentiated at a constant salience, and the budget fits exactly one, so the policy chooses between an evidence claim and its null hypothesis per question. Placement is the third new thing: spliced INLINE into the question sentence rather than added as a labelled block, so it arrives as part of what is being asked.

name: attribute_readout
hypothesis: Every deciding pass in every branch of this run chooses a letter, and 15 of the champion's 49 contested-path errors are recoverable by none of the 24 frameworks here — all of which also choose a letter. So on disagreement, decide once without a ballot: a zero-frame text-only pass synthesises the question that separates the two disputed option TEXTS, one grounded pass answers it in at most eight words over the union of both screens' frames, and the mapping back to a letter is arithmetic — a token counts only if exactly one option in the ballot contains it, with number words folded to digits. Accepted only when exactly one option is named and it is one of the two litigants; anything else is silence and the champion runs untouched. Removes option-slot bias from the decisive step entirely, and is the one attack on Counting (46.8%, worst slice) that needs no detector — numeric_census tried detection and scored 42.6 there.
